subject: CeresHealth dedicated activation: rightsize validation & go-live windows
messages:

To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@cereshealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for CeresHealth — timeline and tests

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We need a concrete activation plan so our infra and procurement teams can sign off on the Dedicated reservation. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm the final GPU count you recommend for our peak and p95 traffic profiles.
- Spell out the acceptance gates (throughput, 99th latency, end-to-end request routing).
- A proposed 2-week cutover window with rollback points and a canary schedule.

We'd like to aim for the first production cutover in the week of Nov 16, but procurement would prefer a slightly later runway if there are unknown risks. Can your team provide a validation checklist and an ops timeline we can attach to our SOW?

Attaching our rough traffic matrix we discussed.

—Maria

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Tim Lee <tim.lee@cereshealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for CeresHealth — timeline and tests

Maria — thanks for the clear asks. I've sketched an operations-forward activation play that balances safety with a two-week target: the attached Excel is our capacity model (v2) and includes both steady-state and burst headroom assumptions. Key points below.

Summary recommendation
- Initial committed pool: 16 x A100 (or equivalent) for the first 30 days, with autoscale burst to 20 for traffic spikes. This maps to your p95 estimate plus 25% safety buffer based on the traffic matrix you sent.
- Canary allocation: 2 GPUs reserved for canary runs in phase 1; ramp to 6 during phase 2.

Acceptance gates (pre-cutover)
- Throughput: sustained 1,200 rps at median response < 120ms and p95 < 420ms across target models during synthetic soak (30m).
- Latency: 99th percentile under 700ms for tail-sensitive routes with cache priming.
- Functional: model variant parity checks, KV cache warm-up, and end-to-end tracing validated in staging.
- Ops: rollback script tested, automated fallback to hosted model variant available.

Cutover windows and rollback points
- Phase 0 (prep): Nov 9–11 — infra provisioning, network peering, KMS config, and initial model push to dedicated images.
- Phase 1 (canary): Nov 16 — run traffic replay for 2 hours on 2 GPUs, validate metrics.
- Phase 2 (incremental ramp): Nov 17–19 — scale to 6 GPUs, A/B traffic 5/95, check regression metrics.
- Phase 3 (full swap): Nov 20 — switch primary traffic to dedicated pool; monitor 24h; rollback allowed until Nov 21 04:00 PST.

I've looped in Ben for detailed throughput numbers and Neha for acceptance criteria. If procurement needs an extra buffer we can shift Phase 1 to Nov 18 without changing the overall ramp plan.

Attachments: capacity_model_v2.xlsx, canary_playbook.md

Next steps
- Ben: confirm sizing math and GPU equivalency for your preferred instance types.
- Neha: expand acceptance checklist with test commands and runbook links.
- Maria/Tim: confirm whether Nov 16 is acceptable for initial canary or if you prefer the Nov 18 fallback.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
[attachment: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-03T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for CeresHealth — sizing notes

Folks — dug into the traffic matrix and simulated a couple of steady/peak scenarios in the spreadsheet. A few technical notes so the ops plan aligns with actual GPU throughput:

Sizing details (short)
- The 16 x A100 recommendation assumes FP16 quantization for the main model and dynamic batching with 50ms batch latency target; if Ceres wants INT8 aggressively, we can reduce to ~12 GPUs but we should validate quality regressions first.
- For the canary profile: run scripted replay at 10% of peak for 30m, then 25% for 30m; this reproduces cache-warm and cold-start behavior.
- Memory headroom: reserve 10% device memory for KV-cache and tracing overhead on each node; recommend monitoring device free memory as an early gate.

Operational caveats
- Network egress: there will be short-lived spikes during model downloads and cache fills; ensure egress throttles or pre-pull images during Phase 0.
- Warm-up: automated prefix caching job should be scheduled 2 hours before canary, not 10 minutes — we observed >30% latency improvement in past runs when cache had time to populate.

I updated capacity_model_v2.xlsx with per-model throughput (tab: model_throughput) and left comments where we should validate INT8 quality. Happy to run a short test on your staging model if you upload a sanitized checkpoint.

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: ceres_vlan_network_diagram.pdf (PDF)]

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for CeresHealth — acceptance checklist and rehearsal slots

Hi Maria / Tim — capturing the acceptance checklist and proposing rehearsal slots so your infra team can block calendars. Full checklist is in the shared Drive link; highlights below are the non-negotiables for go/no-go.

Pre-cutover acceptance highlights
1) Provisioning & Security
  - VPC peering validated and ingress ACLs tested with a signed cert exchange.
  - KMS keys configured and test encrypt/decrypt audited.
2) Functional & Performance
  - Synthetic soak: 1,200 rps sustained for 30 minutes with median <120ms and p95 <420ms.
  - Model parity smoke: 500 sample prompts compared against hosted baseline; token-level divergence within agreed thresholds.
  - Tracing & logging: end-to-end trace IDs surfaced in Redwood Console and linked to your logging sink.
3) Rollback & Fallback
  - Automated fallback rule in routing service verified (route to hosted model instantly).
  - Rollback runbook validated step-by-step with one dry run on Nov 15.

Proposed rehearsal slots:
- Nov 12, 09:00–11:00 PST — provisioning dry run + image pre-pull.
- Nov 15, 22:00–23:30 PST — dry run of rollback and fallback routing.

If those look good we'll finalize dates in the SOW and Ben/Evelyn will join the Nov 12 dry run to validate throughput counters. Maria, can you confirm by EOD Nov 7 whether your infra team can commit to the rehearsal windows? If procurement still wants slack we can shift the canary to Nov 18 and keep the same rehearsal cadence.

Thanks — I added the runbook link here: https://redwoodcorp.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/eng/CeresHealth-Canary-Runbook

Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions Delivery, Redwood Inference
